Study in Ireland

English-speaking, one-year master’s degrees, and a base for many global technology and pharma companies.

Enquire about Ireland Find courses in Ireland

At a glance

Main intakes
September, some in January
Master’s degree
1 year
Bachelor’s degree
3–4 years
English tests
IELTS, PTE, TOEFL or Duolingo
Visa
Study visa

Why students choose Ireland

  • An English-speaking country inside the European Union.
  • Most master’s degrees take one year.
  • Many global technology and pharmaceutical companies have their European offices in Ireland.
  • Graduates can stay on after their course to look for work.

Popular subjects

  • Computer science and cloud
  • Data analytics
  • Pharmaceutical science
  • Finance
  • Business

Documents you will need

  • Passport
  • Class 10, Class 12 and degree mark sheets and certificates
  • English test score
  • Offer letter and fee payment receipt from your university
  • Bank statements or an education loan sanction letter
  • Medical insurance
  • Statement of purpose

After you graduate

The Third Level Graduate Programme lets graduates stay in Ireland after their course to look for work.

Visa and work rules change. Your counsellor will confirm what applies on the date you apply.

Universities in Ireland

See their courses

  • Trinity College Dublin

    Dublin

    Ireland’s oldest university, founded in 1592, in the centre of Dublin.

  • University College Dublin

    Dublin

    Ireland’s largest university. Its Smurfit business school holds triple accreditation.

  • University of Galway

    Galway

    On Ireland’s west coast, in a city that is a centre for medical-device companies.

  • University College Cork

    Cork

    Close to the pharmaceutical and technology companies based around Cork.

  • Dublin City University

    Dublin

    A young university known for its links with employers and paid work placements.

  • University of Limerick

    Limerick

    Known for co-operative education, with a work placement in most degrees.

  • National College of Ireland

    Dublin

    Based in Dublin’s financial district and focused on computing and business.
